rationale: The hypothesis posits that thinning or hypoplasia of the corpus callosum occurs across both missense and loss-of-function (LOF) MAPK8IP3 cohorts rather than being restricted to recurrent missense variants. However, direct evidence for CC thinning specifically in LOF carriers remains ambiguous. Platzer et al. (2019) explicitly observed that corpus callosum hypoplasia and structural brain anomalies were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants rather than truncating variants. While Sudnawa et al. (2026) report corpus callosum thinning in 62.1% of a cohort containing 62.5% missense and 34.4% predicted LOF cases, they note that missense variants cause more severe phenotypes and do not report LOF-disaggregated neuroimaging rates; mathematically, a 62.1% prevalence in a cohort with 62.5% missense cases could be explained by missense cases alone.

evidence.text: Platzer et al. identified de novo MAPK8IP3 variants in 13 individuals (6 missense, 3 of which were recurrent, and 3 truncating) and found that brain anomalies including hypoplasia of the corpus callosum and polymicrogyria were consistent specifically among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants.

source.title: De novo variants in MAPK8IP3 cause intellectual disability with variable brain anomalies
source.quote: Brain anomalies such as perisylvian polymicrogyria, cerebral or cerebellar atrophy, and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants.

evidence.text: Sudnawa et al. evaluated 32 individuals with heterozygous pathogenic MAPK8IP3 variants (62.5% missense, 34.4% predicted LOF) and documented corpus callosum thinning in 62.1% overall, while noting that missense variants generally exhibited more severe phenotypes than LOF variants.

source.title: Comprehensive Clinical Characteristics, Longitudinal Adaptive Functioning, and Electroencephalogram Activity in MAPK8IP3‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder
source.quote: We report on 32 individuals (median age 7.5 years, range 1.3-22.0), all of whom had heterozygous pathogenic/likely pathogenic MAPK8IP3 variants, including missense (62.5%) and predicted loss-of-function (LOF) variants (34.4%)... Corpus callosum thinning was reported in 62.1%.

evidence.text: Iwasawa et al. identified 5 individuals with recurrent de novo missense variants (c.1732C>T and c.3436C>T) in MAPK8IP3 and established corpus callosum hypoplasia as a primary core neurological feature of recurrent missense cases.

source.title: Recurrent de novo MAPK8IP3 variants cause neurological phenotypes
source.quote: We identified 5 individuals from four families with recurrent de novo variants c.1732C>T (p.Arg578Cys) and c.3436C>T (p.Arg1146Cys) in MAPK8IP3. The core phenotype includes spastic diplegia, intellectual disability, cerebral atrophy, and corpus callosum hypoplasia.

evidence.text: Paumier and Gowrishankar review axonal transport disruptions in JIP3/MAPK8IP3 disorders and note that missense mutations may functionally operate via loss-of-function mechanisms leading to thin corpus callosum.

source.title: Disruptions in axonal lysosome transport and its contribution to neurological disease
source.quote: the missense mutations are indeed loss of function mutations ... brain anomalies including thin corpus callosum

conflicts: Platzer et al. (2019) observed that corpus callosum hypoplasia was consistently present among patients with recurrent de novo missense variants, but not highlighted as consistent in truncating/LOF variants.

Sudnawa et al. (2026) report 62.1% corpus callosum thinning overall in a mixed cohort (62.5% missense, 34.4% predicted LOF), but do not provide a separate neuroimaging frequency for the LOF group, leaving open whether thinning occurs at all in non-missense patients.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact MRI prevalence of corpus callosum hypoplasia or thinning in patients with confirmed heterozygous loss-of-function variants (nonsense, frameshift, whole-gene deletion) versus recurrent missense variants in MAPK8IP3?
new_directions.rationale: Existing mixed-cohort studies report aggregate neuroimaging percentages without stratifying callosal anomalies by variant class, obscuring whether LOF alone causes callosal dysgenesis.
